newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh parliament to debate 1997 budget on Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh parliament to debate 1997 budget on Dec 23.

text.p: A joint session of Kazakhstan's parliament plans to debate the oil-rich republic's 1997 budget on December 23, a parliamentary spokesman said on Wednesday.
"The Senate (upper house) and the Mazhilis (lower house) will meet for a joint session on December 23 to debate the budget," the spokesman told Reuters.

Earlier this month, Economy Minister Umirzak Shukeyev told parliamentary deputies that the government of the former Soviet republic planned to increase gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 by 1.5-2.0 percent, up from estimated growth of 0.5-1.0 percent for this year.

Shukeyev, who said the government aimed to raise wages, slow the rise in prices and boost industrial production, estimated the government's budget deficit for 1997 at 3.16 percent of GDP, up from aprroximately 3.0 percent in 1996.
